title: Get Your Calls Reviewed
lede: You will not get good at this alone in a room. Record every call, review it with Jarvis the same day, and bring the hard ones to me.
deliverable: A recorded call, reviewed, and one change for the next one.
body:
Sales is a skill you build by watching yourself do it badly, often, with someone who can tell you why. The people who get good fast turn up to the weekly session with a recording. The ones who stay stuck turn up with a story about one.

Record every call

Every call one and every call two, from the first one you ever do. Tell them at the start, lightly.

Quick one before we start, I record these so I can go back over the details properly rather than scribbling while you talk. All good?

Use whatever your meeting tool does natively. The transcript is what matters, because Jarvis reads transcripts and so do I. Save it to the prospect in your CRM the same day.

Review it with Jarvis within the hour

Here is the transcript of a [call one / call two] I ran today: [paste]. Review it against the course structure. For call one: did I avoid opening with thanks, did I ask the opening question, which branch was it, did I ask the four questions, did I get a dollar figure, did they agree to it out loud, did I pitch or price when I should not have, and did I book call two with the decision makers named? For call two: did I recap in their words and collect yeses, did I present the root cause before the system, did I walk the demo with an exception, did I run the anchoring ladder in order, did I stay silent after the price, and how did I handle the objection? Score each item yes or no with the timestamp and the exact words. Then give me the single biggest thing to change on the next call, and the one thing I did well. Be direct. Do not be kind for the sake of it.

Submit one call a week

Not your best one. The one you are least sure about. Three things.

  1. The recording or transcript.
  2. Jarvis's review, unedited.
  3. One sentence: the moment you want us to look at, with the timestamp.

I listen to the part you flagged, go back to where it actually went sideways, which is usually earlier than you think, and give you one change for the next call. One. You will want five. One is what people actually do.

Keep the changes where Jarvis can hold you to them

Add this to my sales log: on [date] I ran a [call one / call two] with [prospect]. The review said the one thing to change is [the change]. Before each of my next three calls, remind me of this change and the last two before it, and after each call ask me whether I did it.

Record your next call, review it within the hour, send it in with one timestamp. Then book another call, because a review is only useful if there is a next call to use it on.
